# zero-realtime

WebSocket rooms, pools, and cross-core fan-out, and SSE streams with keep-alive comments and Last-Event-ID for zero-server.

[API reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_realtime/index.html) | [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/zero-realtime) | [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-realtime)

## The same capability in every language

| Language | Package | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rust | [`zero-ws`](https://crates.io/crates/zero-ws) | [reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_ws/index.html), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-ws), [install](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust.html#rust-websocket) |
| Rust | [`zero-realtime`](https://crates.io/crates/zero-realtime) | [reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_realtime/index.html), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-realtime), [install](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust.html#rust-websocket) |

The TypeScript, Python and C# packages of this capability ship in a later release.

Real-time connections for zero-server.

`websocket` answers WebSocket handshakes and serves the upgraded connections;
`rooms` groups WebSocket connections for broadcasts that reach every core;
`sse` serves server-sent event streams with keep-alive comments and
`Last-Event-ID`. Connections run on the core that accepted them, claimed from the
HTTP/1.1 driver (`zero_http::takeover`).
